source.title: A Single Neuron Works: Precise Concept Erasure in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
source.authors: Qinqin He; Jia-Qi Weng; Jia-Ling Tao; Hui Xue

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE latent features as units for concept erasure, but does not test the listed claims about neuron-job shares, attribution graphs, or explanations predicting activations on held-out examples.
record.gate_note: The study reports outcomes from suppressing SAE latent features in a text-to-image diffusion model. These findings are about concept erasure by trained SAE features, not audits of native model-neuron poles or tests of the listed versions. Rows below are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"]. Qualitative figures and results cited from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study trains a TopK SAE on Stable Diffusion v1.4 text-encoder activations and suppresses SAE latents to erase concepts. It reports only its method's erasure performance against baselines. It has no audit of native neuron job shares, no cross-model scale sweep, no InceptionV1 analysis, no tool or architecture comparison, no neuron attribution graphs, and no held-out explanation scoring. Its 'neurons' are trained SAE latents, which are the replacement-style units V5 contrasts against.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially correct. The authors conclude that suppressing the top-1 SAE 'neuron' (an SAE latent, not a native neuron) erases target concepts while preserving unrelated content, outperforms prior erasure methods, and is robust to adversarial prompts.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a TopK SAE on Stable Diffusion v1.4 text-encoder activations, selects concept-specific latent features from contrastive prompt pairs, and suppresses them during generation. It does not use the audit or evaluation recipe in the listed claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies neuron-selection setting (top-1, top-10, top-20) and manipulation coefficient λ; it reports that erasure changes with λ and that larger selected sets can alter non-target content when λ exceeds 1.0.

fits_no_version.finding: Suppressing one contrastively selected SAE latent in the SD1.4 text encoder cut I2P nudity detections from 646 to 25 (λ=0.8), with FID 15.85 on COCO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A single SAE latent can serve as a targeted concept-control unit in a text-to-image model's text encoder.

fits_no_version.finding: SNCE lowers attack success rates on I2P user prompts and on the P4D and Ring-A-Bell adversarial sets relative to SD1.4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE-latent suppression reduces measured harmful-content generation, including under adversarial prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: I2P ASR falls from 4.29% to 1.28% as λ rises from 0.6 to 1.2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The erasure effect scales with suppression strength.

record.problems: The experiments use Stable Diffusion v1.4 only. Outcomes are evaluated with automated detectors, no uncertainty estimates are reported, and the study does not test whether identified features predict activation on held-out prompts. The reported interventions target learned SAE latent features rather than native model neurons.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The study's qualitative figure results were not extracted as numerical rows.

untested.parts: All of it: no Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-share estimate.
All of it: only SD1.4 SAE latents, no language-model share across scale or architecture.
All of it: no InceptionV1 or cat-car neuron analysis.
All of it: no comparison of interpretable-neuron share across tools or architectures.
All of it: no attribution graphs built from native neurons. The study uses trained SAE latents instead.
All of it: no test of whether activating-example explanations predict firing on held-out inputs.
All of it: no simulation-based explanation scoring.

record.verdict_notes: The title's 'single neuron' refers to SAE latents, not native model neurons, so the study is not evidence on the neuron-cleanliness claim. All rows are the study's own method versus baselines. Their states should not be 'partial', since no version is attached. The paper's prose about the direction of the λ effect contradicts Table 4.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not estimate the share of neuron poles with one or more jobs, or the share not understood.
It uses Stable Diffusion v1.4, not a cross-model or scale sweep, and does not measure job-share distributions.
It does not examine InceptionV1 or the cat-and-car example.
It does not test the proposed architecture, regularization, or tool explanation of interpretability rates.

It does not build attribution graphs or test whether they explain behaviour without a trained replacement model and reconstruction error. Its SAE features are trained representations, not the model's own neurons.
It does not test whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict activations on new text.
It does not score neuron explanations by simulated activations on new text.
